methods.summary: Create adapter `adapter_name`: its factors, dropout and scale.
methods.extended:
The adapter lives on the base weight's device.  Its dtype is the
base's, except that a float16 / bfloat16 base gets a float32
adapter — the reference's default, which keeps the low-rank update
from underflowing in training.  A layer that holds an adapter already
keeps applying the adapters it applied: the new one is inactive until
`set_adapter` names it.  A layer with none starts applying this one.

Everything the layer cannot do is refused before anything is
allocated or any base weight is touched.

members.summary: An `nn.MultiheadAttention` with LoRA on its input and output projections.
members.extended:
The attention holds its projections as raw parameters and reads them
inside its forward, so the adapter is a change of those weights (see
`_WeightSpace`).  There is no way to adapt one projection alone: each
adapter has a pair of factors for every weight.

* With one fused input projection (`kdim` and `vdim` equal to
  `embed_dim`, no grouped key/value heads) the weights are
  `in_proj_weight` $(3E, E)$ — `lora_A` $(r, E)$,
  `lora_B` $(3E, r)$ — and `out_proj_weight` $(E, E)$ —
  `out_proj_lora_A` $(r, E)$, `out_proj_lora_B` $(E, r)$.
* With separate projections (`kdim` or `vdim` apart from
  `embed_dim`, as in a cross-attention over a context of another
  width, or grouped key/value heads) the query, key and value weights
  each have a pair: `q_proj_lora_*` $(r, E)$ / $(E, r)$,
  `k_proj_lora_*` $(r, E_k)$ / $(E_{kv}, r)$ and
  `v_proj_lora_*` likewise, beside the output projection's.  The reference
  refuses this layout; constructing the layer on such an attention
  returns the layout's own subclass, which is still a
  `MultiheadAttention`.

In an adapter file the tables that the reference would nest under a
module are keyed as it keys them, `....base_layer.out_proj.lora_A.weight`.
The attention's public attributes (`embed_dim`, `num_heads`,
`batch_first`, `in_proj_weight` …) read through to the wrapped
module.  `lora_dropout` is not applied: the update is folded into
the weights, with no activations to drop.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.lora import MultiheadAttention
>>> base = nn.MultiheadAttention(8, 2, batch_first=True)
>>> layer = MultiheadAttention(base, "default", r=2, lora_alpha=4)
>>> tuple(layer.lora_B["default"].weight.shape), layer.embed_dim
((24, 2), 8)
>>> x = lucid.randn(1, 5, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x, x, x)[0] == base(x, x, x)[0]).all().item())   # every B starts at zero
True
>>> cross = nn.MultiheadAttention(8, 2, kdim=6, vdim=6, batch_first=True)
>>> tuple(MultiheadAttention(cross, "default", r=2).k_proj_lora_A["default"].weight.shape)
(2, 6)

methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.

The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

members.summary: An `nn.Conv2d` with a LoRA update: `lora_A` (kernel $k_h \times k_w$, $r$ channels), then `lora_B` (1x1).

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; kept as `base_layer`, its parameters shared.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in `lora_A` / `lora_B`.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.name: lora_dropout
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.name: init_lora_weights
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.name: use_rslora
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.name: use_dora
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

parameters.name: lora_bias
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive and divisible by the base's `groups`.
`init_lora_weights` of `"pissa"` or `"olora"` is refused (the
kernel is not a dense matrix).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.lora import Conv2d
>>> base = nn.Conv2d(3, 5, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
>>> layer = Conv2d(base, "default", r=2, lora_alpha=4)
>>> tuple(layer.lora_A["default"].weight.shape), tuple(layer.lora_B["default"].weight.shape)
((2, 3, 3, 3), (5, 2, 1, 1))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 3, 6, 6)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # B starts at zero
True
notes:
A grouped or depthwise base (`groups > 1`) adapts in the forward pass
(with a warning), but its adapter cannot be merged: a rank-$r$ update
mixes channels across groups, which one grouped kernel cannot hold, so
`merge`, `get_delta_weight` and DoRA raise `NotImplementedError`.  The
reference's convolution LoRA has the same restriction, and the default
targets of the model zoo leave such layers out.  The same holds for
`Conv1d`, `Conv3d` and the transposed layers.

methods.summary: Create adapter `adapter_name`: its factors, dropout and scale.
methods.extended:
The adapter lives on the base weight's device.  Its dtype is the
base's, except that a float16 / bfloat16 base gets a float32
adapter — the reference's default, which keeps the low-rank update
from underflowing in training.  A layer that holds an adapter already
keeps applying the adapters it applied: the new one is inactive until
`set_adapter` names it.  A layer with none starts applying this one.

Everything the layer cannot do is refused before anything is
allocated or any base weight is touched.

methods.name: reset_lora_parameters
methods.summary: Initialise adapter `adapter_name` the way `init_lora_weights` asks.

$B = 0$.  `False`: leave both as the layers made them.

base weight and write the residual back into it, in place.

members.summary: An `nn.Embedding` with a LoRA update: $y = E[x] + s\,(A^\top[x])\,B^\top$.
members.extended:
For an embedding table $E \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times d}$ the factors
are $A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times V}$ and
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}$, kept as bare parameters in
`lora_embedding_A` / `lora_embedding_B` (`....lora_embedding_A.default`
in a state dict, as in the reference).  The update looks the token up in
$A^\top$ — with the base layer's `padding_idx`, `max_norm`,
`norm_type` and `scale_grad_by_freq` — and projects it with
$B^\top$.  Merging adds $s\,(BA)^\top$ to the table.  With
`use_dora` each embedding dimension carries a magnitude (a vector of
`embedding_dim`, normed over the vocabulary); `lora_bias` is not
available on a lookup.

The default initialisation is the reference's: $A = 0$ and
$B \sim \mathcal N(0, 1)$, so the update starts at zero;
`init_lora_weights=False` leaves both normal.  `lora_dropout` has no
place in a lookup and is not applied (a warning says so).

members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with a LoRA update: $y = W x + b + s\,B A\,\mathrm{drop}(x)$.
members.extended:
The base layer runs as it is and stays frozen; the update is computed
in the adapter's dtype and added in the wider of the two dtypes before
the result is cast back to the base output's dtype.  `merge` folds
$s B A$ into $W$ in place, so a merged layer costs what
the base costs; `unmerge` takes it out again.

parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in `lora_A` / `lora_B`.

parameters.description:

positive rank.

parameters.name: lora_alpha

parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input.

parameters.description: Must be `False`: `nn.Linear` stores its weight `(out, in)`.

parameters.name: is_target_conv_1d_layer
parameters.description:
Must be `False`; kept so positional calls line up with the
reference, whose fused-QKV `Conv1D` base v1 does not have.

parameters.name: init_lora_weights
parameters.description:
See `LoraConfig`; `"pissa"` and `"olora"` also rewrite the
base weight (the residual).

parameters.name: use_rslora
parameters.description: Scale by $\alpha/\sqrt r$.

parameters.name: use_dora
parameters.description:
Weight-decomposed update (DoRA): a magnitude vector
(`lora_magnitude_vector`) beside the factors, so the layer computes
$m\,(W + s\,BA)/\lVert W + s\,BA\rVert$ row by row.

parameters.description:
Give `lora_B` a bias (`lora_B.<adapter>.bias`); merging folds it,
scaled, into the base bias.

`r` is not positive, `fan_in_fan_out` or

asks for more rank than the weight has.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.lora import Linear
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", r=2, lora_alpha=4)
>>> layer.base_layer is base, layer.scaling["default"]
(True, 2.0)
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # B starts at zero
True

members.summary: Adapter bookkeeping shared by the LoRA layers.
members.extended:
Holds the wrapped layer as `base_layer` — the very module, so its
parameters stay the same `Parameter` objects (an optimizer, a tied
head and Core ML's identity-keyed weight sharing all keep seeing
them) — and, per adapter name, the rank `r`, `lora_alpha`,
`scaling`, `lora_bias` and `use_dora` and the factor tables
(`lora_A` / `lora_B` and the `lora_dropout` modules in
`ModuleDict`s; `lora_embedding_A` / `lora_embedding_B` in
`ParameterDict`s for an embedding; DoRA's `lora_magnitude_vector`),
so a state dict reads `....lora_A.default.weight` as the reference's
does.  A layer holds any number of adapters, one entry per name in
those tables and in `_specs` (read as the `r`, `lora_alpha`,
`scaling`, `lora_bias` and `use_dora` mappings), and the forward
pass applies the ones named in `active_adapter` that it holds.
Merging folds an update into the base weights in place; each LoRA layer
type supplies the update (`get_delta_weight`) and the forward pass.  A
DoRA adapter folds in as the row-rescaled weight
$m\,(W + sBA)/\lVert W + sBA\rVert$; an adapter with `lora_bias`
also adds its scaled bias to the base bias.

What the forward pass branches on — `active_adapter`,
`disable_adapters`, `merged` — are plain public attributes, not
properties as in the reference: `lucid.compile` keys an executable
on each module's scalar attributes, so state kept anywhere else would
let a compiled model replay the branch of a state it has left
(LCD-703).  They change only through `update_layer`,
`set_adapter`, `delete_adapter`, `enable_adapters`, `merge`
and `unmerge`.

methods.extended:
The result equals the original weights up to the rounding of the

members.summary: A LoRA update on one `nn.Parameter` of a module, for `target_parameters`.
members.extended:
The wrapped module is any module that reads the parameter in its own
forward; the wrapper stands where the module was and calls it with
$W + s\,BA$ read in place of $W$ (see `_WeightSpace`).
Reading the parameter directly (`wrapper.weight`) gives the base
value, the update not applied.  The module's other attributes read
through to it.

A parameter is `(out, in)` — one matrix — or `(experts, out, in)`,
a stack with an adapter pair per expert.  A stack whose module sets
`is_transposed = True` is read as `(experts, in, out)`.  Each
wrapper adapts one parameter; a module with several adapted parameters
is wrapped once per parameter, nested, the outermost standing in the
model.  An adapter file keys the inner wrappers under
`....base_layer.lora_A.weight`.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description:
The module holding the parameter (or the wrapper around it, for a
second parameter); the parameter stays the base model's own.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in `lora_A` / `lora_B`.

parameters.name: parameter_name
parameters.description: Attribute name of the parameter on the module.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive.  `use_dora` and `lora_bias` are
refused, as the reference does.

parameters.name: lora_alpha
parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive.  `use_dora` and `lora_bias` are

parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes

parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes

parameters.description:
The adapter's hyper-parameters, as `LoraLayer.update_layer` takes
them; `r` must be positive.  `use_dora` and `lora_bias` are

parameters.description:

parameters.name: lora_dropout
parameters.description:
Must be 0: the update is folded into the weight, so there is no

raises.description:
`r` is not positive, `lora_dropout` is not 0, the parameter is
missing or is not 2-D or 3-D.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.lora import ParamWrapper
>>> class Gate(nn.Module):
...     def __init__(self) -> None:
...         super().__init__()
...         self.w = nn.Parameter(lucid.randn(4, 6))
...     def forward(self, x):
...         return x @ self.w.mT
>>> gate = Gate()
>>> layer = ParamWrapper(gate, "default", "w", r=2, lora_alpha=4)
>>> layer.get_base_layer() is gate, tuple(layer.lora_A["default"].weight.shape)
(True, (2, 6))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 6)
>>> bool((layer(x) == gate(x)).all().item())   # B starts at zero
True

methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

raises.description:

v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with LoRA.
members.extended:
LoRA (Hu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)) freezes a pretrained weight
$W$ and learns a low-rank update beside it, so a targeted
`nn.Linear` computes $W x + s \, B A x$ with
$A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$,
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ and scale
$s = \alpha / r$ (or $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$ with rsLoRA).

Field names, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference
adapter library's.  Every field is keyword-only.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description:
The task the adapter is for (picks the `PeftModelFor*` class
`get_peft_model` returns; see `TaskType`).

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description: Always `PeftType.LORA`; filled in when omitted.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description:
The class of the base model, `{"base_model_class": name,
"parent_library": module}` — what `AutoPeftModel*` rebuilds the
base with.  `PeftModel.save_pretrained` writes it.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: Name of the model the adapter was trained on (metadata).

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision of that model (metadata).

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too, for inference.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description:
The modules to adapt: `nn.Linear`, `nn.Embedding`,
`nn.Conv1d` / `nn.Conv2d` / `nn.Conv3d`, their
`nn.ConvTranspose` counterparts and `nn.MultiheadAttention`;
the module's type picks the LoRA layer that wraps it
(`lucid.peft.tuners.lora`).  A list matches a module whose
dotted name equals an entry or ends with `"." + entry`; a string
is a regular expression the whole name must match; `"all-linear"`
selects every `nn.Linear` except the output head and any layer
whose weight is shared with another module.  `None` takes the
default for the base model's `model_type`
(`DEFAULT_LORA_TARGET_MODULES` in `lucid.peft._target_defaults`);
a model type with no row raises `ValueError`.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description:
Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head);
a trainable copy is kept and saved with it, the original stays.
An entry matches a module whose dotted name equals it or ends
with `"." + entry` — on a dot boundary, so `classifier` does
not also catch `pre_classifier` as the reference's bare suffix
test does.  Nothing inside these modules is adapted.

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description:
Adapt only these layer indices (the number after the layer list's
name, `transformer.h.3.attn` → 3).  Applies to modules matched
by suffix; one named in full is adapted regardless.  The index is
the reference's current rule: the first (outer) `<list>.<n>.` in
the name, so `encoder.layers.0.blocks.1.qkv` is layer 0.  A
layer list at the model's root (`h.3.attn`) is indexed too,
where the reference finds no index without a `layers_pattern`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
r
parameters.description: Rank of the update.

parameters.name: lora_alpha
parameters.description: $\alpha$ in the scale.

parameters.name: lora_dropout
parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input, in `[0, 1)`.

parameters.name: fan_in_fan_out
parameters.description:
For bases that store their weight `(in, out)`.  `nn.Linear`
does not, so `True` warns and is reset to `False`.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
Which biases also train: none, every parameter named `bias`, or
only the biases of the adapted layers.

parameters.name: use_rslora
parameters.description: Scale by $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$ (Kalajdzievski, 2023).

parameters.name: init_lora_weights
parameters.description:
`True`: Kaiming-uniform $A$ (`a = \sqrt 5`) and zero
$B$, so the adapted model starts as the base.
`"gaussian"`: $A \sim \mathcal N(0, 1/r^2)$, zero
$B$.  `False`: both keep `nn.Linear`'s initialisation
(the update is non-zero from the start — for tests).
`"pissa"` (Meng et al., 2024) puts the weight's top-$r$
singular components into $BA$ and the residual into the base
weight; `"pissa_niter_<k>"` does it with a randomised SVD of `k`
power iterations.  `"olora"` (Büyükakyüz, 2024) puts the first
$r$ columns of a QR decomposition's $Q$ and rows of
$R$ there instead.  Both **rewrite the base weight in place**
(the adapted layer still starts as the original), so an adapter
trained from them is relative to that rewritten base — save one
with `save_pretrained(..., path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion=)`
to get a plain LoRA of twice the rank that fits the original base;
they apply to `nn.Linear` targets only.  `"eva"`, `"corda"`, `"loftq"` and
the reference's other initialisations raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: rank_pattern
parameters.description: Per-module rank overrides, keyed by name or regex suffix.

parameters.name: alpha_pattern
parameters.description: Per-module $\alpha$ overrides, keyed the same way.

parameters.name: use_dora
parameters.description:
Weight-decomposed low-rank adaptation (Liu et al., 2024): a trainable
magnitude per output unit beside $BA$, so the adapted weight
is $m\,(W + sBA)/\lVert W + sBA\rVert$ row by row.  Supported
on `nn.Linear`, `nn.Embedding` and the convolutions (not grouped
ones); `nn.MultiheadAttention` and `target_parameters` refuse it,
as the reference does.  Costs a norm of the full weight per forward
pass; merge before inference.

parameters.name: target_parameters
parameters.description:
Raw `nn.Parameter`s to adapt, for a parameter that no layer
reads through a module of its own (an attention's fused
`in_proj_weight`, a mixture-of-experts weight stack).  An entry
matches a parameter whose dotted name equals it or ends with
`"." + entry`.  The parameter is `(out, in)`, or a stack of
them, `(experts, out, in)`; `lora_dropout` must be 0 for it.
The holding module cannot also be in `target_modules`.  With no
`target_modules`, no module is adapted (the model-type default is not taken).

parameters.name: lora_bias
parameters.description:
Give $B$ a bias, folded into the base bias on merge.  For
adapters extracted from a fully fine-tuned layer; needs
`init_lora_weights` of `True` or `False` and not `use_dora`.
`nn.Linear` and convolutions only.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A field is out of range or two fields conflict.
An `init_lora_weights` the library lacks (`"eva"`, `"loftq"` …).

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=4, lora_alpha=8, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"])
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q_proj', 'v_proj'], <PeftType.LORA: 'LORA'>)
>>> LoraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True
>>> dora = LoraConfig(use_dora=True, init_lora_weights="PiSSA_niter_4")
>>> dora.use_dora, dora.init_lora_weights
(True, 'pissa_niter_4')

methods.name: __init__
methods.summary: Adapt `model` in place, building LoRA's low-rank factors as `adapter_name`.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: LoRA updates off, original `modules_to_save`.
methods.extended:
With `bias` other than `"none"` the trained biases are base
parameters and stay as trained, so the output is not the base
model's; a warning says so.

methods.name: add_weighted_adapter
methods.signature: add_weighted_adapter(adapters: list[str], weights: list[float], adapter_name: str, combination_type: _CombinationType = 'svd', svd_rank: int | None = None, svd_clamp: float | None = None, svd_full_matrices: bool = True, svd_driver: str | None = None, density: float | None = None, majority_sign_method: Literal['total', 'frequency'] = 'total')
methods.summary: Add an adapter that is a weighted combination of existing ones.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is frozen and inactive, like any added adapter, and
has $\alpha = r$, so its scale is 1 and the weights live in
its matrices.  It targets the union of the sources' modules; a
layer one source does not reach combines the sources it has.

parameters.name: adapters
parameters.description: Names of the adapters to combine.

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: One weight per adapter; negative weights subtract.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter.

parameters.name: combination_type
parameters.description:
`"svd"`: the rank-`svd_rank` truncation of
$\sum_i w_i s_i B_i A_i$.  `"cat"`: that sum exactly,
at the sum of the ranks.  `"linear"`: `A` and `B` weighted
apart (adding cross terms $B_i A_j$); one rank.  With one
adapter every type is `"linear"`.  `"ties"`, `"dare_linear"`,
`"dare_ties"` and `"magnitude_prune"` (which take a
`density`) merge `A` and `B` apart; their `*_svd` forms
merge the updates and truncate like `"svd"`.  TIES trims to the
largest elements and elects a sign; DARE drops elements at random
(`lucid.manual_seed` repeats it) and rescales.

parameters.name: svd_rank
parameters.description: Rank of an `"svd"` result; the largest source rank by default.

parameters.name: svd_clamp
parameters.description:
A quantile in `[0, 1]`; `"svd"` factors are clamped to the
symmetric range holding that share of their values.

parameters.name: svd_full_matrices
parameters.description: Whether the SVD computes full `U` / `Vh`.

parameters.name: svd_driver
parameters.description: The SVD routine; `lucid.linalg.svd` accepts `None` only.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description:
The share of elements to keep, in `[0, 1]`; required by the
TIES, DARE and magnitude-prune types.

parameters.name: majority_sign_method
parameters.description:
How TIES elects an element's sign: that of the sum, or the one
most adapters have.

raises.description:
The name is taken, a source does not exist, the weights do not
match the sources, they cannot be combined that way (the factor
types need one rank; two train one `modules_to_save` module),
`combination_type` is unknown, or a type that prunes got no
`density`.
A source is a DoRA or `lora_bias` adapter.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, LoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(6, 5))
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> lora = LoraModel(net, config, adapter_name="a")
>>> lora.add_adapter("b", config)
>>> lora.add_weighted_adapter(["a", "b"], [0.5, 0.5], "mix", combination_type="cat")
>>> net[0].r["mix"]
4

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.signature: add_adapter(adapter_name: str, peft_config: PeftConfig, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False)
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — the config class of this tuner's method.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature.  There is no meta
device to build the adapter on: it is allocated either way.

raises.description:
The name is taken or malformed, the config is another
method's, no module matches it, or it cannot sit beside the
adapters held (two adapters training biases).
`peft_config` is not an adapter config.

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)
methods.summary: Apply the named adapter(s) in the forward pass, and train exactly those.
methods.extended:
Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter, or adapters, to apply.

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the activated adapters too.

raises.description:
A name is not one of the model's adapters, or two named
adapters train the same `modules_to_save` module.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: set_requires_grad(adapter_names: str | Sequence[str], requires_grad: bool = True)
methods.summary: Enable or disable gradients on the parameters of the named adapter(s).

raises.description: A name is not one of the model's adapters.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the adapted model; its adapter layers do their work inside the call.

methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description:
Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.  A layer holding
only some of them merges those.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or the adapter is
disabled (inside `disable_adapter()`).

A name is not one of the model's adapters, or `safe_merge`
found a non-finite merged weight.

methods.name: unmerge_adapter
methods.summary: Take every merged adapter update back out of its base weight.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; there is no progress bar.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

methods.name: enable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Apply the adapter again after `disable_adapter_layers`.

members.summary: A model with LoRA layers put into it, and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each module `config` selects with a LoRA layer
around it — `lucid.peft.tuners.lora.Linear`, `Embedding`,
`Conv1d` / `Conv2d` / `Conv3d` or `MultiheadAttention`, by the
module's type — each module holding a parameter `target_parameters`
names with a `lucid.peft.tuners.lora.ParamWrapper` for that
parameter, and each `modules_to_save` entry with a frozen-original /
trainable-copy pair, then freezes every other parameter.  The model is
changed in place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper
lacks is read from it.  `config` itself is not changed:
`peft_config` holds a copy, with `"all-linear"` spelled out as the
names it chose.

The model can hold any number of adapters, each under its own name:
`add_adapter` puts another beside the first (frozen and inactive),
`set_adapter` chooses which one — or which several — the forward pass
applies, `add_weighted_adapter` makes one out of others and
`delete_adapter` removes one.  `active_adapter` is the name, or the
list of names, in use.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules` (and no parameter
`target_parameters`), a match is a module type with no LoRA
layer, `modules_to_save` matches nothing, or the model already
holds adapters of another method or one named `adapter_name`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, LoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> lora = LoraModel(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> lora.targeted_module_names
['0']
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].lora_A["default"].weight.requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> lora.add_adapter("other", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> lora.active_adapters, sorted(lora.peft_config)
(['default'], ['default', 'other'])
>>> lora.set_adapter("other")
>>> lora.active_adapters, net[0].lora_A["default"].weight.requires_grad
(['other'], False)
>>> lora.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

warns.description:
The model already holds LoRA adapters: the new one is added beside
them and becomes the one in use (the earlier ones are frozen), as
`get_peft_model` does on a model it adapted before.

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.lora` — LoRA: a low-rank update learned beside each frozen weight.
extended:
LoRA (Hu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)) freezes a pretrained weight $W$ and learns a
rank-$r$ update next to it, $y = W x + s\,B A x$ with $s = \alpha / r$.  $B$
starts at zero, so the adapted model starts as the base, and the update folds into $W$ on
merge.  It is the method to start with: it has a layer for every common module type and the
widest set of options — DoRA (`use_dora`), rsLoRA, PiSSA and OLoRA starts, per-module ranks and
alphas, and combining adapters (`add_weighted_adapter`).

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, LoraLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.lora import Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type per module the method
adapts: `Linear`, `Embedding`, the convolutions `Conv1d` / `Conv2d` / `Conv3d` and their
transposes `ConvTranspose1d` / `ConvTranspose2d` / `ConvTranspose3d`, `MultiheadAttention`,
and `ParamWrapper` for a raw parameter. `LoraConfig` and `LoraModel` are defined here too and
exported from `lucid.peft`, which is where `get_peft_model` is.  Importing the package registers
the method (its config under `PeftType.LORA`, its tuner and layers), which is what makes
`get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Hu, Edward J., et al. "LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models." [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685), 2021.
theory:
LoRA (Hu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)) freezes a pretrained weight
$W$ and learns a low-rank update beside it, so a targeted
`nn.Linear` computes $W x + s \, B A x$ with
$A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$,
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ and scale
$s = \alpha / r$ (or $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$ with rsLoRA).
